RAP-001.check: Google OAuth (amr oauth): first protected request records one session.observed for the verified subject and one alert decision

RAP-002.check: email OTP (amr otp): first protected request records one session.observed for the verified subject and one alert decision

RAP-003.check: passkey (amr webauthn): first protected request records one session.observed for the verified subject and one alert decision

RAP-004.check: POST /api/auth/verify (bootstrap) before GET /api/me: exactly one observation and one alert

RAP-005.check: GET /api/me then POST bootstrap: a single first-observed event across both routes

RAP-007.check: a workspace API as the very first request: the verifier observes it, and its session checks run before any data

RAP-008.check: GET /api/me ten times (cold process each time): one first-sighting event, one mail

RAP-009.check: parallel first requests (verifier, /api/me, sessions list, workspace) on one new session: one event, no deadlock

RAP-010.check: a refreshed JWT (new iat, same session_id) records no new sign-in

RAP-011.check: a verified JWT without a session_id claim: 401 on every session route, zero rows, no substitute session

RAP-012.check: a forged userId/sessionId in a request body is ignored: the row belongs to the verified subject only

RAP-013.check: the session's security record cannot be written: no allowed state, and the protected route answers 503
RAP-013.detail: AssertionError: refused with 403 security_step_up_required instead of 503
RAP-013.knownGap: an unrecordable security state refuses the protected capability with 403 step-up, not 503

RAP-014.check: first authenticated browser request without a device cookie: the server issues an opaque host-only cookie and records an `observed` device

RAP-015.check: no token, an expired token and a token getUser refuses: every security endpoint answers 401, no data

RAP-017.check: same browser, new session: the session is new, the device is the existing one; no new device claim

RAP-018.check: a new browser profile for an existing account: a new device record, a device.first_observed event and an eligible alert

RAP-019.check: person B signs in on person A's browser: B gets an unrelated device record; A's device and trust are untouched

RAP-020.check: a copied device cookie without a JWT: 401, no device row, no data

RAP-021.check: a stolen device cookie plus a valid AAL1 JWT still needs fresh proof for a sensitive action (trust alone is not sufficient)
RAP-021.detail: AssertionError: a known cookie plus an AAL1 bearer reached a sensitive capability without fresh proof
RAP-021.knownGap: a copied device cookie plus an AAL1 bearer reads as a known browser: sensitive capabilities need no fresh proof

RAP-022.check: malformed or overlong device cookies: no crash, treated as no cookie, a fresh one is issued, no trust

RAP-023.check: the device Set-Cookie is __Host- prefixed, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ and has no Domain (never shared with a parent or old domain)

RAP-024.check: a client claiming a native surface gains nothing: the device stays surface=web, state=observed

RAP-025.check: a private window (no cookie) on a known account: a separate observed device with a clear browser label

RAP-026.check: the browser's cookie expired: the next session is an unknown browser and a sensitive capability needs fresh proof

RAP-027.check: HMAC key rotation: a cookie hashed under the old key is recognised, re-hashed under the new key, and not trusted

RAP-028.check: a revoked device's cookie replayed after a new sign-in: the old record stays revoked and a new untrusted record is made

RAP-031.check: known browser, no recent change, AAL2: an ordinary view and a sensitive capability are both allowed

RAP-032.check: unknown browser: account security and ordinary views stay open, a sensitive capability asks for proof

RAP-033.check: unknown browser right after a sensitive account change: the private drafts list answers 403 security_step_up_required
RAP-033.detail: AssertionError: private workspace state served with 200
RAP-033.knownGap: only four capabilities are gated (tokens, connections, Agent grants, exports); private drafts stay readable

RAP-034.check: a fresh same-inbox email OTP is not an independent factor: step-up still required

RAP-035.check: a fresh verified TOTP on an AAL2 session: allowed, and the step-up is recorded on this session

RAP-036.check: TOTP older than the step-up window: refused; a refreshed token (new iat) is not new proof

RAP-037.check: a WebAuthn MFA ceremony is verified from the signed token; a client boolean proves nothing

RAP-038.check: a passkey first-factor sign-in (AAL1) is not treated as AAL2 step-up

RAP-039.check: an account hold blocks a sensitive capability even from a known browser with fresh AAL2 proof
RAP-039.detail: AssertionError: export served under an active hold (200)
RAP-039.knownGap: the step-up gate does not consult account holds: a held account's interactive session can still export

RAP-040.check: riskLevel=low / trusted=true in the request is ignored: the challenge stands

RAP-041.check: a different country header on a known browser never locks the account; ordinary reads continue

RAP-042.check: spoofed X-Forwarded-For / geo headers are never stored or used in a decision

RAP-043.check: a stale stored decision is never reused: the request is re-evaluated under the current policy first

RAP-044.check: security state unreadable: the sensitive capability fails closed with 503; ordinary and help routes still work

RAP-045.check: an account with no second factor gets a deterministic enrolment/recovery next step, not an unsatisfiable MFA prompt
RAP-045.detail: AssertionError: nextAction=complete_mfa for an account with no factor
RAP-045.knownGap: an account with no second factor is told to complete MFA it cannot complete (no enrolment/recovery next step)

RAP-046.check: a second factor removed after the proof: the old proof no longer authorizes a sensitive action
RAP-046.detail: AssertionError: a TOTP proof from before the factor was removed still authorized the export
RAP-046.knownGap: a fresh TOTP proof from before the factor was removed still satisfies step-up

RAP-047.check: a direct API client with no Security Center code meets the same challenge

RAP-048.check: proof made in session B never satisfies session A

RAP-049.check: DELETE /api/auth/sessions/{own other}: that session is denied, the current one keeps working

RAP-050.check: DELETE of another person's session id: the same 404 as an unknown id, and B's session unchanged

RAP-051.check: repeating DELETE on an already revoked session: same safe response, no second audit row

RAP-052.check: a revoked session's still-valid access JWT: 401 on the next hosted API request, no data

RAP-053.check: the same revoked JWT straight through the Data API (authenticated role + JWT claims): reads no workspace row

RAP-054.check: the revoked JWT cannot list private Storage objects (the signing step reads storage.objects under the same guard)

RAP-055.check: POST revoke-others: every other session denied, the current one valid, the count exact

RAP-058.check: revoking the current session through the API takes effect at once (the UI offers no revoke button for it)

RAP-059.check: revocation fence in both orders: a write after the revocation commits nothing; a write before it stands alone

RAP-060.check: one revocation applies to the person in every workspace they belong to

RAP-061.check: a valid API token is refused at the action gateway while the account is held

RAP-062.check: account protection flag off: a revoked session stays denied (core revocation does not depend on RAPv2)

RAP-063.check: alert preference off: the sign-in is in the account history, and no routine mail

RAP-064.check: a high-risk security event queues a mandatory notice even with routine alerts off
RAP-064.detail: AssertionError: an incident report (hold placed, sessions revoked) produced no security notice for the person
RAP-064.knownGap: risk decisions and incidents queue no mandatory notice

RAP-065.check: alert preference on: the sign-in is in the account history, and exactly one routine mail

RAP-066.check: alert preference off: the sign-in is in the account history, and no routine mail

RAP-067.check: one eligible sign-in with Notification V2 on: the legacy mailer stands down and V2 sends exactly one email; with V2 off the legacy mailer sends exactly one

RAP-068.check: transport failure: the event and audit stay, retries are bounded with backoff, then the delivery is dead (not dropped)

RAP-069.check: provider accepted is `sent`, never `delivered`, until the provider's delivered webhook arrives

RAP-070.check: the same provider callback twice (and concurrently): applied once, no second email

RAP-071.check: two delivery workers ticking at once: one lease, one send, one idempotency key

RAP-078.check: a bounce receipt: the delivery is failed and email suppressed (visible to operations), never delivered

RAP-079.check: anon: no SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on any session-security table (P0 and P1)

RAP-080.check: authenticated: no direct write on any session-security table, and no read of other people's or person-level rows

RAP-081.check: the service role performs the expected session writes and reads

RAP-082.check: every session-security table has RLS enabled and FORCED (a table with no policy is deny-all to non-bypass roles)

RAP-083.check: pr_session_security cannot link person A's session to person B's device (composite foreign key)

RAP-085.check: person A never sees person B's incidents, and B's incident is unchanged

RAP-086.check: user A cannot read or command workspace B through the hosted API (membership check)

RAP-087.check: sign-in events are append-only: no role (authenticated, service_role) may UPDATE or DELETE pr_audit_events

RAP-088.check: account deletion removes the person's session inventory and redacts their sign-in history (no session id or browser label)

RAP-089.check: two concurrent first-sighting inserts of one session: exactly one first observation

RAP-090.check: re-evaluations with new event keys are all kept; the same key twice is one row

RAP-091.check: the user id written for a session or revocation is always the verified token subject

RAP-092.check: the P1 migrations (120-123) apply to a disposable database: every table and function exists, RLS forced

RAP-093.check: work approved before the hold (and the hold since released) is refused at worker claim

RAP-094.check: a hold placed after the worker claimed (epoch captured) stops the final pre-publish check

RAP-095.check: hold set, released and set again: a job holding the old epoch is refused (no ABA)

RAP-096.check: reconnecting a social account from a challenged session needs fresh proof

RAP-097.check: a viewer's direct publish/approve call is refused by role, whatever the browser

RAP-098.check: an Agent/worker run prepared before the owner removed the grant is denied on the refreshed membership

RAP-099.check: a held account's scheduled/proactive phone call is refused before any provider call

RAP-101.check: a valid API token is refused at the action gateway while the account is held

RAP-102.check: a consumer session reaches no founder/operator API on the consumer app

RAP-104.check: turning the incident/hold feature flag off after an incident keeps the core hold enforced
RAP-104.detail: AssertionError: the held account's API token worked again (200) once RAFII_SECURITY_INCIDENT_HOLD was off
RAP-104.knownGap: turning RAFII_SECURITY_INCIDENT_HOLD off stops enforcing existing holds

RAP-105.check: GETs of the Security Center's data (me, sessions, security events) never revoke, hold or change factors

RAP-106.check: an unconfirmed (cancelled) report changes nothing: no hold, no revocation

RAP-107.check: a confirmed report with fresh proof: one incident, the hold epoch moves, a receipt says what was done

RAP-108.check: an anonymous or forged report: 401 and no hold

RAP-109.check: reporting another person's sign-in event: the same 404 as an unknown id, no incident, no hold

RAP-110.check: a repeated report with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same receipt; no second hold

RAP-114.check: an incident notifies previously verified contact channels
RAP-114.knownGap: an incident report sends no notice to any contact channel

RAP-115.check: the incident receipt says already-executed actions are not reversible and connected accounts were not disconnected

RAP-116.check: following an email link (GET) without confirming in the app changes nothing

RAP-132.check: probing the incident route with foreign or random ids gives one generic 404 body

RAP-133.check: 200 sign-ins in a burst with alerts on: notices are bounded, every event is retained

RAP-134.check: a report from a hostile Origin is refused by the origin guard before anything changes

RAP-135.check: the device Set-Cookie is __Host- prefixed, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ and has no Domain (never shared with a parent or old domain)

RAP-138.check: a browser unused for more than 180 days is no longer silently known
RAP-138.detail: AssertionError: a browser idle for 200 days still counted as known
RAP-138.knownGap: a browser idle for 200 days still reads as known (no inactivity expiry)

RAP-139.check: flag absent (default off): legacy behaviour — sessions recorded as before, no session.observed, no new friction

RAP-140.check: observe mode: sign-ins are recorded and an ordinary read is not challenged; existing guards unchanged (AAL1 still refused under 2FA)

RAP-141.check: enforce mode turns the gate on for protected operations; observe mode leaves them as before

RAP-142.check: the experimental v2 flag turned off after the revocation: a revoked session stays denied (core revocation does not depend on RAPv2)

RAP-143.check: notification provider outage: the sign-in request does not wait on mail transport and the event is durable

RAP-144.check: security state unreadable: connecting an account (the step before any connected publish) fails closed with 503

RAP-146.check: one eligible sign-in with Notification V2 on: the legacy mailer stands down and V2 sends exactly one email; with V2 off the legacy mailer sends exactly one

RAP-147.check: the harness refuses any target but the dedicated local disposable cluster

RAP-150.check: rollback (observe → off): revoked sessions stay revoked and recorded sign-ins stay in the history
